name: Theodosius I
title: Theodosius the Great
summary: Theodosius I, also known as Theodosius the Great, was Roman emperor from 379 to 395. He won two civil wars and was instrumental in establishing the Nicene Creed as the orthodox doctrine for Nicene Christianity. Theodosius was the last emperor to rule the entire Roman Empire before its administration was permanently split between the Western Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman Empire. He ended the Gothic War (376–382), but did so on terms disadvantageous to the empire, with the Goths remaining politically autonomous within Roman territory, albeit as nominal allies.
notes: Reign: 15 years, 11 months and 29 days. The division of the empire at Theodosius's death (395) is traditionally dated as the beginning of separate Western and Eastern Roman histories. He was the last emperor to rule both halves. | Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodosius_I
